assessment.nobel_worthiness: Pd-catalyzed C-N cross-coupling turned aryl amine construction from a harsh, narrow-scope problem into a routine operation. It is among the most used bond-forming reactions in medicinal and process chemistry, and the ligand-design logic (bulky, electron-rich phosphines) generalized well beyond amination. What was new chemically is clear: a general catalytic C(sp2)-N bond formation.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general, ligand-enabled catalytic methods independently and in parallel in the mid-1990s and then led the ligand generations that made the reaction broadly usable. Kosugi's earlier tin-amide coupling is a precursor, not the general method, so a two-person prize is defensible but his priority could be raised.
assessment.maturity: About three decades of validation, with ubiquitous use in pharma and materials. Recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: The 2010 prize on Pd cross-coupling may make the committee view this as a continuation of already-recognized chemistry.
Weight given to Kosugi's precursor work versus the ligand-enabled general methods is a judgment call.
I have not independently verified exact priority dates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Visible-light photoredox catalysis opened radical and open-shell pathways under mild conditions, enabling bond constructions that were impractical by polar chemistry, including metallaphotoredox cross-couplings. It is now routine in discovery chemistry and increasingly in process settings. The conceptual simplicity (a photocatalyst as a single-electron shuttle) is attractive.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread across several groups around 2008-2009 (MacMillan, Yoon, Stephenson, Nicewicz) with earlier photochemistry by Fukuzumi and others and strong later contributions from König and Melchiorre. A three-person prize is possible but any choice leaves out significant contributors. MacMillan is already a laureate (2021, organocatalysis), which may weigh against him.
assessment.maturity: Broad independent adoption within about 15 years and clear industrial uptake. Some reaction classes remain still maturing.
uncertainties: Distribution of credit among founders is genuinely contested.
Prior laureate status of MacMillan could change the optimal configuration.
Long-term industrial scalability of some photochemical processes is still being established.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective C-H functionalization, through directing-group, ligand-controlled and template strategies, addresses the efficiency problem directly: it shortens syntheses by avoiding pre-functionalization and allows late-stage modification. Yu's ligand-accelerated approaches to site-selective C-H activation are a notable conceptual advance, and the field has real uptake in total synthesis and pharma.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand-enabled Pd C-H functionalization, remote/meta selectivity), Hartwig (Ir-catalyzed borylation, with Smith) and Sanford (Pd/high-oxidation-state catalysis) each made distinct decisive contributions. Smith and Daugulis also have claims, so a three-person selection is a compromise.
assessment.maturity: Impactful and growing, but selectivity and generality are still uneven and industrial use, while real, is less ubiquitous than for cross-coupling. Perhaps slightly early for a unified citation.
uncertainties: It is unclear whether the committee would honor one unifying principle or several separate methods.
Scope limitations and reliance on directing groups may be seen as not yet routine.
Crediting a subset of contributors is delicate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Isolable stable carbenes upended the view of carbenes as transient species and led to N-heterocyclic carbenes becoming ubiquitous ligands and organocatalysts, notably in olefin metathesis catalysts and in cross-coupling. The conceptual shift is clear and its downstream use in synthesis is wide.
assessment.attribution: Arduengo's 1991 crystalline NHC is the decisive discovery; Bertrand's earlier phosphinocarbenes (1988) and later cyclic alkyl amino carbenes are a major independent contribution. Nolan's role is mostly on the catalysis application side. Credit allocation between discovery and application is arguable.
assessment.maturity: Over 30 years of confirmation and broad adoption. Recognition is mature.
uncertainties: Priority between Bertrand's 1988 work and Arduengo's isolable NHC may be argued.
Whether application-driven contributors such as Nolan belong beside the discoverers is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Phosphoramidite chemistry made reliable automated oligonucleotide synthesis possible, underlying PCR primers, sequencing, gene synthesis and all oligonucleotide therapeutics. Pure chemistry with enormous leverage on biology, and a classic efficiency-driven method.
assessment.attribution: Caruthers developed the phosphoramidite method in the early 1980s and is the clear central figure. Hood is credited on automation and instrumentation, which is a different contribution and is not needed for a chemistry prize on the method itself.
assessment.maturity: Decades of universal use make this very mature, and a risk is that it is arguably overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as chemistry-level priority over later biological applications.
Credit for solid-phase predecessors (Letsinger, Khorana-era work) may be raised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation provides chemoselective peptide-bond formation between unprotected segments, making total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins practical. It is a clear methodological advance in chemistry with applications from protein engineering to chemical biology.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson reported the 1994 method; Muir extended it to expressed protein ligation, which brought it into semisynthesis of large proteins. This gives a sensible three-person structure. Danishefsky's desulfurization-related work is a lesser claim.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely used in protein chemistry for about 30 years, though it remains a specialist tool rather than a universal one.
uncertainties: Breadth of use outside specialist labs may be judged modest.
Contributions from Liu, Brik and Danishefsky could complicate the configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Frustrated Lewis pairs showed that sterically encumbered acid-base pairs activate H2 and other small molecules without metals, a new concept in main-group reactivity that led to metal-free hydrogenation catalysis. Conceptually elegant, though practical impact on how chemists make molecules is so far limited.
assessment.attribution: Stephan's 2006 metal-free H2 activation is the founding report; Erker's later work on intramolecular and reactive FLPs is a major contribution. A two-person prize is clean.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups, but synthetic utility is still small compared with transition-metal catalysis, so it may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Practical use in industry is limited.
Priority claims (e.g. earlier related work) are uncertain to me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion with orthogonal aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase/tRNA pairs allows site-specific incorporation of unnatural amino acids in cells. The chemical novelty is in the design of the unnatural residues and orthogonality, and it has broad application in protein engineering and chemical biology. As a synthetic chemist I would ask whether the discovery is chemical or biological engineering.
assessment.attribution: Schultz established the approach in the early 2000s; Chin extended it with orthogonal ribosomes and quadruplet codons and to multicellular organisms. Wang and Yokoyama also made important contributions, so exclusions are significant.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely adopted in research, with some therapeutic translation.
uncertainties: The border between chemistry and biology may reduce its standing for a chemistry prize.
Credit among Schultz, Wang, Chin and Yokoyama is not easily resolved.
